 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal
 Order
% 22.03.2023 Exemption allowed subject to just exceptions.
This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.65/2023 dated 02nd March, 2023 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC lodged at PS Anand Vihar, New Delhi.

The learned counsel for the petitioner states that this is the third FIR being lodged by the same complainant arising out of matrimonial issues, the earlier two FIRs being Nos.306/2022 and 524/2022 against which quashing petitions have been filed viz. W.P.(CRL) 2755/2022 and W.P.(CRL) 3132/2022 which have also listed before this Court.
Ld. ASC accepts notice and will file a status report before the next date of hearing.

3. As noted in the order dated 09th January, 2023 passed by this Court in W.P.(CRL) 3132/2022,
the Ld. Standing Counsel had stated that no coercive steps will be taken till the next date of hearing subject to petitioner cooperating with the investigation.

Learned counsel for the petitioner states that they have not been served any notice as regards this FIR No.65/2023 and undertake to fully cooperate with the investigation, as and when summoned by the IO.
4. Further in the said order dated 09th January, 2023, the issue had been raised by the petitioner that multiple FIRs cannot be registered on the same transaction between the parties.
It is noted that while these previous writ petitions were pending before this Court a third FIR has been filed by the complainant arising out of similar matrimonial issues.

The State has already been directed to consider the facts relating to these multiple FIRs and may advert to the same in view of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala, (2001) 6 SCC 181 and Surender Kaushik v. State of U.P., (2013) 5 SCC 148.
